summary: The agent created an Excel workbook but the verifier failed, indicating insufficient validation. This skill captures reusable patterns for Excel workbook creation with openpyxl, including environment setup for externally-managed Python environments and critical verification steps that go beyond file existence checks.

Updated excel-workbook-creation skill to add critical formula syntax pitfalls discovered in the trace: SUM range syntax errors (SUM(B6:8) vs SUM(B6:B8)), formula reference debugging when cells point to wrong rows, and clarification that data_only=True returns None for uncached formulas. These were the actual bugs the agent had to fix during execution.

The agent created a workbook with correct structure but wrong column references - formulas linked to column O (Coverage Months) instead of column N (Sep Ending Balance). The verification was superficial, checking formula existence but not formula correctness. Adding guidance on column mapping verification and formula logic validation.

The agent created a workbook with correct structure but wrong control row logic: GL Balance row had formulas instead of hardcoded GL values, Variance formula was backwards, and summary sheet linked to wrong columns. The existing skill covers general Excel creation but lacks explicit guidance for reconciliation spreadsheets where control rows have specific requirements (GL Balance must be hardcoded, Variance must compare calculated to GL). Adding a dedicated section for reconciliation control rows with verification checklist.

The agent created a workbook where the summary sheet linked to column O (Useful Life Months) instead of column N (Sep Ending Balance). The existing skill has column mapping guidance but lacked explicit verification patterns for summary sheet links. Adding a dedicated verification section for summary-to-detail links will help future agents catch this common off-by-one error before declaring success.

The agent made the exact mistake the skill warns about - linking summary sheet to column O (auxiliary column) instead of column N (ending balance column). The skill's guidance was correct but not followed. Adding explicit verification step for summary sheet column references and clarifying that the column mapping rule applies to ALL summary links, including control rows.

The agent created a workbook with multiple formula errors that weren't caught by verification: (1) GL Balance row had formulas in auxiliary column O instead of hardcoded values, (2) Variance formulas were missing from ending balance columns and only present in column O with wrong logic, (3) Summary links pointed to column O (formula) instead of column N (hardcoded GL Balance). The skill needs expanded verification to check ALL columns in GL Balance row, verify Variance formulas exist in all period columns, and validate summary links point to hardcoded values.

The trace shows the agent made the exact mistakes the skill warns about: linking summary to column O (auxiliary) instead of N (ending balance), putting Variance formulas only in column O instead of ending balance columns, and putting formulas in GL Balance row. The skill already documents these anti-patterns, but the verification section needs strengthening to make these checks more prominent and harder to miss. Adding explicit verification checklist items for these specific issues.

The agent made the exact 'column O trap' error that the skill warns about - linking summary sheets to column O (Amortization Months) instead of column N (Apr Ending Balance). Additionally, the GL Balance row had formulas in column O instead of hardcoded values, and Variance was only in column O instead of each ending balance column. The skill already documents these anti-patterns but they're buried in a long document. This update adds a prominent 'Most Common Errors' section at the top and a quick verification snippet to catch these mistakes before declaring success.
